analyst_view.overall: Early view: second-placed Brighton, the league's top scorers with 26 goals, host David Moyes's Everton, who are sixth and coming off wins over Newcastle and Coventry. Brighton are in the Conference League and host Monaco on Thursday 10 December, then go to Panathinaikos the following Thursday, so Fabian Hurzeler may rotate; Everton have no European games. One report says Jack Grealish is unavailable for disciplinary reasons with no timeline given.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. Brighton score plenty at home (5-0 wins over Coventry and Palace) but have also kept three clean sheets in a row, and Everton under Moyes are hard to break down. With rotation after Monaco possible, nothing points clearly either way.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.0 corners. I lean higher: Brighton keep the ball and attack down the flanks, and Everton usually defend deep and clear wide under Moyes, which tends to give up corners.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards. Everton are physical, with James Tarkowski at the back, but Brighton games are usually controlled rather than heated. The referee is not yet known, so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.9 shots, already high and heavily weighted to Brighton. A rotated Brighton side after the Monaco game could take a little less, so I stay at the number rather than above it.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target. I lean slightly lower: against a deep block at Getafe, Brighton won 1-0 in a game with only seven shots on target in total, and Everton under Moyes defend in a similar way.
